newsitem.title: USA: Tropical Storm Kyle heads for Central America.
newsitem.headline: Tropical Storm Kyle heads for Central America.

text.p: Tropical Storm Kyle emerged in the western Caribbean on Friday and was expected to buffet Honduras, Belize and the Yucatan Peninsula with gusty winds and rain, the National Hurricane Center said.
Kyle had maximum sustained winds of 50 mph (80 kmh) and was located 65 miles (105 km) southeast of Belize City at 11 p.m. EDT (0300 GMT Saturday), hurricane forecasters said.
The storm's position was latitude 16.9 north and longitude 87.5 west, and it was drifting west at 3 mph (5 kmh). It was expected to continue moving in the same way on Saturday.

"We think it could get a little bit stronger before it moves over northern Central America and Mexico," said hurricane center forecaster Miles Lawrence, adding that the storm was moving so slowly it could be Saturday evening before its center made landfall.

The National Hurricane Center said a tropical storm warning, indicating that storm conditions could arrive within 24 hours, was recommended from Felipe Carrillo Puerto on the Yucatan Peninsula southward and eastward to Cabo Camaron, Honduras, including Belize and adjacent islands.
A hurricane watch, indicating the possible arrival of hurricane conditions within 36 hours, was recommended for Felipe Carrillo Puerto to the border of Guatemala and Honduras.

A small storm, with tropical storm force winds extending outward up to 60 miles (95 km), Kyle grew out of stormy weather left behind by last week's Tropical Storm Josephine, which pushed through northern Florida and along the U.S. eastern seaboard.
"The circulation around Josephine is what pushed a lot of cold air southward, and that's the front which settled into the northwestern Caribbean and helped form Kyle," Lawrence said.
Forecasters warned that rainfall associated with Kyle could be especially heavy because the storm was moving so slowly, saying that the storm could bring as much as 15 inches (37.5 cm).
Kyle would become a hurricane if maximum sustained winds reached 74 mph (119 kph).
